newsitem.title: GERMANY: Higher German grain crop possible - Toepfer.
newsitem.headline: Higher German grain crop possible - Toepfer.

text.p: Germany's 1997 grain crop may amount to 43 million tonnes, compared with 42.1 million last year, grain trader Toepfer said in a market report on Friday.
The trader said the forecast was preliminary and assumed normal weather.
It cited good crop development, but added that the wheat harvest would be delayed.
Last month, Toepfer's market report said German farmers may have to cut earlier projections for a larger 1997 harvest to 42 million due to lower yields.
The wheat crop in 1997 could total 19 million tonnes, broadly unchanged from last year, Toepfer said.
It pegged barley at 12.7 million tonnes (12.1 in 1996), rye at 4.3 million (unchanged), maize at 2.8 million (2.9) and triticale at 2.7 (2.1).
The rest of the total comprised oats and mixed grains, for which no specific forecasts were available.
